target.title: fix(cli): keep root help descriptions aligned with registered commands
target.body:
Fixes #98978

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw --help` renders root command descriptions from static descriptor catalogs, while `openclaw <command> --help` and shell completion use the live registered commands. Those two sources had drifted apart, which made root help disagree with command help and completion output.

The drift was not just wording churn. Some root descriptions were materially misleading, especially `config`, whose root help line hid shipped `patch` and `schema` subcommands.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes the descriptor catalogs the canonical source for top-level command descriptions and updates the catalog entries to match the current live command behavior.

It also synchronizes top-level command descriptions back onto the registered commands after lazy or eager command-group registration. That keeps these surfaces aligned:

- `openclaw --help`
- `openclaw <command> --help`
- shell completion

This keeps the startup-friendly placeholder catalogs while removing the long-term drift between placeholder metadata and live command registration.

## User Impact

CLI users now see the same top-level command descriptions across root help, command help, and completion.

This fixes misleading discovery text for commands like:

- `config`
- `setup`
- `onboard`
- `doctor`
- `status`
- `gateway`
- `daemon`
- `secrets`

In particular, root help now correctly advertises `config` as supporting `patch` and `schema`.

## Evidence

Targeted regression tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts src/cli/program/register.subclis.test.ts
```

Diff sanity:

```bash
git diff --check
```

Local CLI proof after the patch:

```text
openclaw --help
config * Non-interactive config helpers
(get/set/patch/unset/file/schema/validate). Run without
subcommand for guided setup.
```

```text
openclaw config --help
Non-interactive config helpers (get/set/patch/unset/file/schema/validate). Run
without subcommand for guided setup.
```

What was verified locally:
- root help now shows the corrected `config` summary
- `openclaw config --help` shows the same top-level description
- regression tests cover the command-group registration path that now re-applies descriptor-catalog descriptions after lazy/eager registration

What was not fully captured as standalone terminal proof:
- a clean completion stdout snippet from the local Windows wrapper path, although completion uses the same eagerly registered top-level command tree that now receives the synchronized catalog descriptions

target.title: fix(process): resolve gemini .cmd shim on Windows in supervisor child adapter
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- On Windows, using the `google-gemini-cli` provider fails with `spawn gemini ENOENT` because Node's `child_process.spawn` does not automatically resolve `.cmd` extensions (only `.exe`/`.com`)
- npm global installs on Windows create `.cmd` shim files, so `gemini` (and `claude`) need the `.cmd` suffix to be found by `spawn`
- Fixes #98573

## Why This Change Was Made

The supervisor child adapter (`src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts`) has a `resolveCommand` function that uses `resolveWindowsCommandShim` with a hardcoded allowlist of commands that should get `.cmd` appended on Windows. The list included `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, and `npx` but not `gemini` or `claude` — so spawning those CLI tools failed on Windows.

## User Impact

- Windows users can now use the `google-gemini-cli` and `claude-cli` providers without encountering `ENOENT` spawn errors
- No change on macOS or Linux (platform guard already skips non-Windows)

## Evidence

### Behavior or issue addressed
- On Windows, `spawn("gemini")` fails with ENOENT because Node only auto-resolves `.exe`/`.com` extensions, not `.cmd`
- The `resolveCommand` helper was missing `gemini` from its shim allowlist

### Real environment tested
- Local development environment (Linux, Node 22)
- Unit tests simulate Windows platform via `setPlatform("win32")` to verify cmd.exe wrapping behavior

### Exact steps or command run after this patch
```bash
pnpm test src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts
```

### Evidence after fix
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  21 passed (21)
```

New regression tests added:
- `wraps gemini CLI command through trusted cmd.exe on Windows (#98573)` — verifies `gemini` → `gemini.cmd` wrapped via `cmd.exe` on Windows
- `wraps claude CLI command through trusted cmd.exe on Windows` — verifies `claude` → `claude.cmd` wrapped via `cmd.exe` on Windows
- `keeps gemini command unchanged on non-Windows platforms (#98573)` — verifies no `.cmd` suffix on Linux/macOS

Existing test `wraps Windows command shims through trusted cmd.exe` (for `pnpm`) already validates the same code path — the new entries follow the identical pattern.

### Observed result after fix
- On simulated Windows: `spawnArgs.argv` = `[cmd.exe, /d, /s, /c, "gemini.cmd --version"]` (shim resolved)
- On Linux: `spawnArgs.argv` includes `gemini` verbatim (no `.cmd` suffix)

### What was not tested
- Not tested on a real Windows machine (no Windows environment available). The unit tests use `setPlatform("win32")` to simulate the Windows code path and verify the exact spawn arguments.

## Tests and validation

```bash
pnpm test src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts  # 21 tests pass (was 18, +3 new)
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] No: Does this change affect user-visible behavior? (Only affects Windows CLI tool spawning, restoring expected behavior)
- [x] No: Does this change affect configuration surface?
- [x] No: Does this change affect security? (No change to security model; same pattern used for other CLI tools like pnpm/npm/yarn)
- [x] No: Does this change affect plugin APIs?
- [x] No: Does this change require documentation updates?

## Additional notes

AI-assisted fix. Similar to how `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, and `npx` were already handled, `gemini` and `claude` now also get the `.cmd` shim resolution on Windows. The `resolveWindowsCommandShim` function in `src/process/windows-command.ts` already handles the platform check and extension detection — the only missing piece was the allowlist entry.

The sibling PR #98609 targets the same issue with a similar approach. Compared to that PR, this one also covers `claude` (which has the same Windows spawn issue) and includes tests for the non-Windows path.
